title: The Economics of SaaS (Software as a Service)

parts.visual:
Why does Wall Street love SaaS (Software as a Service)? Because it replaces one-time sales with predictable, recurring revenue.

The Holy Trinity of SaaS Metrics:
1. MRR/ARR: Monthly/Annual Recurring Revenue.
2. Churn Rate: The percentage of customers who cancel their subscription.
3. CAC Payback Period: How many months it takes to earn back the money you spent to acquire the customer.
parts.audio: SaaS business models are built on recurring revenue. Executives track MRR, the Churn Rate, and the CAC Payback Period obsessively.

questions.question: You have an amazing marketing team that signs up 1,000 new users every month. However, your 'Churn Rate' is 20% a month. What is the executive analysis?
options: The business is a 'Leaky Bucket'. You are spending millions to acquire users who hate the product and leave immediately. Fix the product before doing more marketing.
questions.correct_answer: The business is a 'Leaky Bucket'. You are spending millions to acquire users who hate the product and leave immediately. Fix the product before doing more marketing.
questions.explanation: High churn is the number one killer of SaaS companies. It means the product is failing to deliver value.

questions.question: Listen to the CFO. What metric are they complaining about?
questions.tts_text: We spend $100 to acquire a user, but they only pay us $10 a month. It takes 10 full months just to break even on them!
questions.explanation: If it takes 10 months to pay back the acquisition cost, and the customer churns in month 6, the company loses money on every single sale.

questions.question: Why do investors value ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue) so much higher than one-time sales revenue?
options: Because recurring revenue is highly predictable. Predictability lowers risk, which drastically increases the valuation of the company.
questions.correct_answer: Because recurring revenue is highly predictable. Predictability lowers risk, which drastically increases the valuation of the company.
questions.explanation: A company making $10M in unpredictable one-time sales might be worth $15M. A SaaS company with $10M in ARR might be worth $100M.

questions.question: What is 'Negative Churn'?
options: The holy grail of SaaS: When the extra money generated from existing customers upgrading their accounts is greater than the revenue lost from customers cancelling.
questions.correct_answer: The holy grail of SaaS: When the extra money generated from existing customers upgrading their accounts is greater than the revenue lost from customers cancelling.
questions.explanation: Negative churn means your company will grow revenue every year even if you never sign a single new customer.
